RSYC model update plan: v20260709 to v20260923

Source: MODEL_UPDATE_V20260923_PLAN.md

Copy-ready prompts for executing this plan in separate chats are available in MODEL_UPDATE_V20260923_PROMPTS.md.

Purpose

This document is a self-contained implementation handoff for updating the RSYC R package from model release v20260709 to v20260923.

The package repository is K:\_PROJECTS\RSYC. The authoritative model products are under:

K:\_PROJECTS\RSYC-Canada\outputs\products\models\versions\v20260923

The objective is to merge the existing local-calibration work into dev, make the model update on a dedicated branch from dev, and leave main unchanged until the associated paper is published.

Git workflow

At the time this plan was written:

  • local-calibration is exactly one commit ahead of dev.
  • local-calibration and dev have not diverged, so a fast-forward merge is appropriate.
  • main must remain frozen for the paper.
  • dev is the integration branch containing current development work.
  • RSYC_package_description.md is an untracked file and must be preserved or deliberately added/ignored before unrelated cleanup.

Merge local calibration into dev:

git switch dev
git merge --ff-only local-calibration
git push origin dev

Create a pre-update reference tag:

git tag -a pre-model-v20260923 -m "Dev with local calibration before v20260923 model update"
git push origin pre-model-v20260923

Create the model-update branch:

git switch -c model-v20260923 dev
git push -u origin model-v20260923

All model-update pull requests should target dev, not main. Keep main protected from direct pushes and do not merge dev into main until the paper is published.

Suggested implementation commits:

  1. Update model import contract for v20260923
  2. Import v20260923 model catalogue
  3. Update ecological and tile boundaries
  4. Update tests and documentation for v20260923

For scientific traceability, prefer a normal PR merge commit into dev if the individual commits are clean.

Confirmed model contract changes

Contract v20260709 v20260923
Rows 28,391 28,043
Columns 38 42
Model version v20260709 v20260923
Shared lookup keys 21,999 21,999
Shared keys with changed curve coefficients - 21,991
Old-only lookup keys - 6,392
New-only lookup keys - 6,044

The four new columns are:

ecozone_id
ecoprovince_id
ecoregion_id
ecodistrict_id

The curve equation remains:

b1 * exp(-b4 * age) * (1 - exp(-b2 * age))^b3

The v20260923 source has:

  • unique model_id values;
  • valid UTF-8 character data;
  • finite curve coefficients;
  • publish_ok == TRUE for all included rows;
  • positive finite local_b1_var and residual_var for all national rows;
  • the same b1 and parent-random-effect semantics required by calibrate_rsyc().

Prediction and local-calibration logic are therefore structurally compatible with the new model table.

Numeric eco-strata selection API

The v20260923 model table adds identifiers for every level of the ecological hierarchy. Users should be able to select models using these identifiers as an alternative to ecological names and full hierarchical paths.

Identifier characteristics

The identifiers are codes, not quantities. Preserve their source types and do not perform arithmetic on them.

Strata level Source field Source type Unique within level?
Ecozone ecozone_id integer No
Ecoprovince ecoprovince_id character codes such as "10.1" Yes
Ecoregion ecoregion_id integer Yes
Ecodistrict ecodistrict_id integer Yes

Ecoprovince identifiers should remain character codes internally and in outputs. Accepting a numeric value such as 10.1 as input is a convenience, but documentation should recommend the quoted form "10.1" so formatting is preserved if the upstream coding scheme later gains multi-digit or zero-padded components.

Ecozone IDs are not always unique because some official numeric zones are represented by named package subdivisions:

Ecozone ID Matching names
5 Taiga Shield East, Taiga Shield West
6 Boreal Shield East, Boreal Shield West
10 Subhumid Prairies, Semiarid Prairies

Calls requiring one model must report these as ambiguous rather than silently choosing the first match. The error should list the matching names and instruct the user to select by name or full path. Discovery functions may return all matches for an ambiguous code, just as catalogue filtering can return multiple models; this distinction should be explicit and tested.

Public API design

Add a new optional argument named strata_code rather than overloading the existing strata_id argument. In the existing API, strata_id means a tile ID, ecological name, or hierarchical name path. Keeping numeric codes separate makes validation, documentation, and ambiguity messages clearer.

Support strata_code in:

predict_rsyc()
calibrate_rsyc()
available_rsyc_models()
rsyc_species()
build_rsyc_dataset()

rsyc_strata() does not need a code filter initially, but it must return the code so users can discover available values. A future code filter can be added consistently if useful.

For backward compatibility:

  • retain the position and meaning of strata_id;
  • add strata_code = NULL at the end of public signatures where possible;
  • where selection by code requires omitting a formerly required strata_id, make strata_id = NULL and require later arguments such as observations to be supplied by name;
  • preserve all existing name- and path-based calls unchanged.

Require exactly one of strata_id and strata_code for functions that select one or more specified strata. Reject calls supplying both. For catalogue functions, both may remain NULL to mean no geographic filter.

Examples of the intended interface:

predict_rsyc(
  response = "agb",
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  age = c(40, 80),
  strata_level = "ecoregion",
  strata_code = 198
)

calibrate_rsyc(
  response = "volume",
  species = "PICE.MAR",
  strata_level = "ecodistrict",
  strata_code = 134,
  obs_age = c(45, 70),
  obs_response = c(110, 145)
)

available_rsyc_models(
  response = "agb",
  strata_level = "ecoprovince",
  strata_code = "10.1"
)

build_rsyc_dataset(
  response = "agb",
  species = c("PICE.MAR", "POPU.TRE"),
  strata_level = "ecoregion",
  strata_code = c(198, 208),
  age = c(50, 100)
)

strata_code is not applicable to strata_level = "tile"; tile selection continues to use strata_id and values such as "H14". Return an informative error if a code is supplied for tiles.

For functions where strata_level is optional, require exactly one ecological level when strata_code is supplied. The same textual code can occur at different ecological levels, so matching it across all levels would be surprising and potentially unsafe.

Internal representation and resolver

Add one internal helper that maps a level to its source identifier column:

.rsyc_strata_code_field <- function(strata_level) {
  switch(
    strata_level,
    ecozone = "ecozone_id",
    ecoprovince = "ecoprovince_id",
    ecoregion = "ecoregion_id",
    ecodistrict = "ecodistrict_id",
    NULL
  )
}

Add a shared code normalizer and resolver used by prediction, calibration, catalogue filtering, and dataset building. It should support an explicit single-match versus multi-match mode and should:

  1. Accept non-missing finite numeric values or non-empty character codes.
  2. Convert values to a canonical character representation for comparison.
  3. Compare only against the identifier column for the requested level.
  4. Return the corresponding canonical name/path stored in strata_id.
  5. Report an unknown-code error when no matching stratum is available for the requested response/species context.
  6. In single-match mode, report an ambiguity error listing every matching name/path when a code maps to more than one available stratum.
  7. In multi-match discovery mode, return all matching strata deterministically.

Do not implement this as four independent code paths. The existing .rsyc_select_model(), .rsyc_filter_models(), and .rsyc_resolve_dataset_strata() logic should delegate to the same resolver so selection behavior and error messages remain consistent.

Discovery and output columns

Expose a level-specific canonical strata_code column in:

  • available_rsyc_models();
  • rsyc_strata();
  • the curves result from build_rsyc_dataset();
  • the spatial result from rsyc_boundaries() and build_rsyc_dataset().

For a row at a given strata_level, strata_code is drawn from the matching source field. For example, an ecoregion row uses ecoregion_id. Keep the four raw hierarchy ID fields in RSYC_models for advanced users and provenance.

Ecological boundary layers should preserve all available hierarchy ID fields. rsyc_boundaries() may return both the convenient target-level strata_code and the raw ancestor/current ID fields, but the exact public column contract must be documented and tested. Tile boundaries should return strata_code = NA only if a uniform cross-level schema is considered valuable; otherwise omit it for tiles and document that tile IDs remain in strata_id.

Identifier API tests

Add tests covering:

  1. Numeric ecoregion and ecodistrict codes select the same model as the corresponding full path.
  2. Quoted ecoprovince codes such as "10.1" select the same model as its path.
  3. A numeric ecoprovince input such as 10.1 is normalized consistently.
  4. rsyc_strata() and available_rsyc_models() expose the expected strata_code values.
  5. Vector codes work in build_rsyc_dataset() and preserve requested order or the package’s documented canonical order.
  6. Supplying both strata_id and strata_code errors.
  7. Supplying neither errors in single-model functions.
  8. Supplying strata_code for tiles errors.
  9. Supplying a code without exactly one ecological strata_level errors in catalogue filters.
  10. Unknown codes produce an actionable message.
  11. Ambiguous ecozone codes 5, 6, and 10 produce an error listing both matching names in prediction, calibration, and dataset construction.
  12. A unique ecozone code resolves successfully.
  13. Catalogue discovery with an ambiguous ecozone code returns both matching strata rather than silently dropping one.
  14. Boundary and model strata_code values agree for every published national ecological stratum.
  15. Existing name, short-name, full-path, and tile-ID behavior remains unchanged.

Corrected national-model coverage findings

PINU.BAN and ABIE.LAS have selected national models in the current v20260923 product for both responses and both geographic families:

  • ecological-strata AGB;
  • ecological-strata volume;
  • tile AGB;
  • tile volume.

They must not be listed as missing.

Using the v20260709 previous indicator joined to the current authoritative v20260923 selection_report.csv, there are 10 national-model coverage losses:

Geography Response Species Current selection reason
Ecological strata AGB ALNU.INC All candidates ineligible
Ecological strata AGB LARI.LAR All candidates ineligible
Ecological strata AGB QUER.RUB All candidates ineligible
Ecological strata Volume ALNU.INC All candidates ineligible
Ecological strata Volume FRAX.NIG No candidate models
Ecological strata Volume LARI.LAR All candidates ineligible
Ecological strata Volume QUER.RUB All candidates ineligible
Tiles AGB LARI.LAR All candidates ineligible
Tiles Volume FRAX.NIG All candidates ineligible
Tiles Volume LARI.LAR All candidates ineligible

These species are considered lower priority for this package update, but the coverage changes should still be documented in NEWS.md.

The current package artifact contains the following examples of confirmed national coverage:

  • ABIE.LAS: 66 tile curve rows for AGB and 66 for volume, plus ecological curves at all four levels.
  • PINU.BAN: 145 tile curve rows for AGB and 145 for volume, plus ecological curves at all four levels.

Implementation steps

1. Centralize the release contract

Create one release configuration used by the import, export, tests, and boundary-build scripts. It should contain at least:

  • model version;
  • upstream Git commit;
  • source RDS path or environment-variable convention;
  • source RDS SHA-256;
  • expected row and column counts;
  • expected column names and types;
  • boundary version;
  • boundary source and checksums.

This avoids repeating release-specific constants in multiple scripts.

Current hard-coded locations include:

data-raw/import_rsyc_models.R
data-raw/export_rsyc_models.R
data-raw/build_ecostrat.R
tests/testthat/test-data.R
R/data.R
NEWS.md
inst/ECOSTRATIFICATION.md

2. Update the model importer

Update data-raw/import_rsyc_models.R to use the v20260923 source.

The old importer contains a v20260709-specific Latin-1 repair and regenerates 270 model IDs. Do not apply that workaround to v20260923. The new source is valid UTF-8 and already contains unique stable IDs.

The importer should:

  1. Read the authoritative RDS.
  2. Verify its SHA-256 and upstream version.
  3. Verify 28,043 rows and 42 expected columns.
  4. Verify the expected column types.
  5. Verify unique model_id and lookup keys. Do not incorrectly require ecozone_id to be unique; instead validate the documented one-to-many mappings for IDs 5, 6, and 10.
  6. Verify responses, units, scale values, strata levels, and equation.
  7. Verify publish_ok, finite coefficients, and positive national calibration variances.
  8. Preserve upstream model_id values unchanged.
  9. Save data/RSYC_models.rda using the existing package data format.

The default source path may point to the sibling RSYC-Canada project, while continuing to support RSYC_MODELS_SOURCE for reproducible overrides.

3. Update the model export

Update data-raw/export_rsyc_models.R for the new version, dimensions, and 42-column schema. Regenerate:

data/RSYC_models.rda
data-raw/RSYC_models.zip
data-raw/RSYC_models_manifest.csv

The manifest should record more than the output ZIP checksum. Prefer including:

  • model version;
  • upstream Git commit;
  • source RDS SHA-256;
  • output ZIP SHA-256;
  • archive member;
  • row and column counts;
  • build time.

Retain the CSV round-trip checks for IDs, version, schema, and coefficients.

4. Rebuild ecological boundaries as a new boundary release

The current ecological boundary file is not sufficient for v20260923.

Current versus new model-aligned boundary counts are:

Layer Current v20260923
Ecozones 12 17
Ecoprovinces 101 44
Ecoregions 257 154
Ecodistricts 936 721

The current boundary file lacks geometry for model paths introduced in the new catalogue, including 5 ecozones, 8 ecoprovince paths, 17 ecoregion paths, and 60 ecodistrict paths. Without rebuilding it, build_rsyc_dataset() will fail for valid new models at its missing-geometry check.

Update data-raw/build_ecostrat.R to:

  • use v20260923 as the source model version;
  • declare a new boundary version, recommended v2;
  • expect the new layer counts;
  • accept and preserve the four ecological ID fields;
  • verify that model and boundary identifier mappings agree;
  • validate EPSG:3978, geometry validity, UTF-8, layer names, fields, and join keys;
  • write a deterministic artifact and checksum manifest.

Use a versioned cache filename such as:

RSYC_ecostrat_v2.gpkg

This prevents an existing cached v1 file from colliding with the new checksum. Update R/ecostrat.R, tests, documentation, URL, and checksum accordingly.

The published URL should eventually use an immutable release or tag rather than the current dev branch URL.

5. Decide and document the tile-boundary policy

The current bundled tile file contains 389 tile IDs. It covers every tile ID needed by the new national model catalogue but includes four IDs no longer used by the new models:

D34
E35
P1
R1

The new upstream GeoPackage has 649 tile feature rows but only 385 distinct model join keys. Do not copy that layer directly into the package: multiple features must be dissolved by join_key to obtain model-aligned tile polygons.

Preferred approach:

  1. Extract the tiles layer from the v20260923 GeoPackage.
  2. Dissolve geometries by join_key.
  3. Validate 385 unique non-missing keys and EPSG:3978.
  4. Write a package-compatible RSYC_tiles.gpkg with one row per tile.
  5. Update boundary tests from 389 to 385 rows.

Alternatively, retain the current tile file after documenting that it covers all new model keys. Rebuilding is preferred because it provides clean v20260923 provenance and removes the four retired tiles.

6. Remove obsolete special handling

The v20260923 catalogue no longer contains the previously hidden invalid ecodistrict path:

Taiga Shield West/Keewatin Lowlands/Dubawnt Lake Plain/Upland

Review and preferably remove the release-specific filter in R/utils.R and its associated tests. General catalogue validation should replace a hard-coded exception where possible.

7. Update package version and documentation

Recommended package version while developing:

0.2.0.9000

Use 0.2.0 for the eventual release. This update changes predictions, model availability, the public model-table schema, and boundary products, so a minor version is more appropriate than a patch.

Update source documentation:

DESCRIPTION
NEWS.md
R/data.R
inst/ECOSTRATIFICATION.md
README.Rmd, where applicable
vignettes/articles/Model-parameters.Rmd
vignettes/articles/Local-calibration.Rmd

Document the four new ID columns and the corrected coverage changes. Re-render calibration examples because their numerical results will change with the new coefficients.

Add user documentation and examples for selecting by strata_code, including the ambiguous ecozone IDs and the recommendation to quote ecoprovince codes.

Regenerate rather than hand-edit:

man/
docs/
README.md and README.html when generated from README.Rmd

8. Update tests

Update the model contract tests for:

  • 28,043 rows;
  • 42 columns;
  • version v20260923;
  • the four new ecological ID columns;
  • unique IDs and lookup keys;
  • valid UTF-8;
  • finite coefficients and positive calibration variances.

Implement the identifier API tests listed in the numeric eco-strata selection section. Update existing exact-column-name assertions for the new strata_code discovery and dataset outputs.

The existing tests were run in memory against the new table. Prediction and calibration logic were compatible. Expected fixture changes included:

  • the old row, column, and version assertions;
  • tests expecting the short ecological name Muskwa to be ambiguous, which is no longer true for the relevant new catalogue subset.

Add an exhaustive boundary compatibility test for every public level:

all unique national model strata_id values must occur in the corresponding
boundary layer

Also test that boundary join keys are unique after any tile dissolve.

9. Validate the completed update

Required validation gates:

  1. Source checksum and upstream Git commit recorded.
  2. Exact schema and type contract passes.
  3. No duplicate model IDs or lookup keys.
  4. All published coefficients are finite.
  5. All national calibration variances are finite and positive.
  6. Every national model stratum joins to exactly one boundary geometry.
  7. Model, catalogue, and boundary code-to-path mappings agree.
  8. Exported CSV round-trips without meaningful coefficient changes.
  9. devtools::document() completes.
  10. devtools::test() passes.
  11. R CMD check --as-cran passes.
  12. Package site and vignettes build successfully.
  13. Smoke tests cover AGB and volume, tiles and ecological strata, prediction, local calibration, and GeoPackage dataset export.

Representative smoke-test species should include PINU.BAN, ABIE.LAS, PICE.MAR, and a broad species group. Each ecological smoke-test workflow should be exercised once by name/path and once by strata_code, with identical model IDs and predictions expected.

Completion and merge

When all validation gates pass:

git push origin model-v20260923

Open a pull request from model-v20260923 into dev. After merging:

git switch dev
git pull --ff-only origin dev
git branch -d model-v20260923

Keep main unchanged. When the paper is published, merge the validated dev branch into main, create the formal package release, and add the final version tag.

Instructions for a future implementation chat

Start by reading this file, checking git status, confirming the active branch, and rechecking the modification times and checksums of the authoritative v20260923 inputs. Do not trust the stale summary comparison’s selected field. Use the current product selection_report.csv and the actual rsyc_models_rpackage.rds as the primary model-selection and package-data sources. Implement the numeric eco-strata API through the shared resolver described above; do not assume ecozone IDs are unique.
